Sole external reference: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.13548 (Sharma et al., 'Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models', Anthropic, 2023), independently re-fetched live 2026-07-10 -- abstract quotes in the maintainer Source-verification block match the primary source verbatim, not a drifted paraphrase. Citation correctly carries [academic/research] label, correct freshness stamp grammar ([checked:2026-07-02 result:OK due:2027-01-02]), and is explicitly flagged 'dated-foundational' to justify citing >6mo-old research for a durable mechanism claim rather than a decaying benchmark -- fits the freshness rule's own historical-context carve-out. curriculum/evals/scripts/source-freshness.sh --target 2026-07-10 confirms the file raises neither BLOCK nor WARN. The nine-in-ten/seven-steps cascading-error arithmetic is explicitly labeled 'an illustration, not a measurement' in body and is arithmetically correct (0.9^7 = 0.4783 < 0.5, independently recomputed) -- zombie-stat guard satisfied by design. No Claude Code / Anthropic product-capability claims in this file at all (the LLM-training description is generic pretraining+preference-tuning architecture, not a vendor-specific feature assertion); no [Skill: ...] references; no Quality stamp present (file is correctly unaudited by design per its own STATUS line, so no SHA-pin to verify). File is confirmed wired into scripts/build-workbook.js's THEORY_HANDBOOK_MANIFEST and linked from getting-going.md / trainer-modules.md / training-architecture.md, matching its maintainer-block placement claim. No prompt content at all means check_prompts.md's 44 rules are uniformly N/A for this file; check_pedagogy's technical subset (16/22/23/36/37) is also uniformly N/A -- this is a pure-prose theory lecture (lede + 3 slides + kicker), not an exercise/module with forcing-function or verification-machinery architecture. Zero blocking findings. One non-blocking, purely optional suggestion logged below.
